fields.name: episode_id
fields.description: the unique identifier of the episode (data format: text)

fields.name: series
fields.description: the name of the series (data format: text)

fields.name: season
fields.description: a number indicating the season of the episode (data format: integer)

fields.name: episode
fields.description: the sequential number of the episode within a specific season (data format: integer)

fields.name: number_in_series
fields.description: the overall sequence number of episode in the entire series (data format: integer)

fields.name: title
fields.description: the title of the episode (data format: text)

fields.name: air_date
fields.description: the date the episode was initially broadcast in the United States

fields.name: rating
fields.description: the weighted average of the votes received for the episode commonsense evidence: The higher rating means the episode has more positive viewer comments. (data format: real)

fields.name: votes
fields.description: the total number of rating votes for the episode (data format: integer)

fields.name: person_id
fields.description: the unique identifier for the person (data format: text)

fields.name: name
fields.description: the name of the person (data format: text)

fields.name: birthdate
fields.description: the date the person was born if null, it means this birthdate of the person is not available

fields.name: birth_name
fields.description: the name parents gave to the person shortly after birth (data format: text)

fields.name: birth_place
fields.description: the place where a person was born. commonsense evidence: the birth place info is integrate if birth_name, birth_place, birth_region don't contain null value the full birth place = birth_country +birth_region +birth_place (data format: text)

fields.name: birth_region
fields.description: the geographical area describing where a person was born that is larger than the birth place (data format: text)

fields.name: birth_country
fields.description: the name of the country where the person was born commonsense evidence: can ask questions about its corresponding continent: e.g.: USA --> North America (data format: text)

fields.name: height_meters
fields.description: how tall the person is in meters (data format: real)

fields.name: award_id
fields.description: the unique identifier for the award nomination (data format: integer)

fields.name: organization
fields.description: the name of the organization that grants the award (data format: text)

fields.name: year
fields.description: the year of the nomination for  the award (data format: integer)

fields.name: award_category
fields.description: the class of the award (data format: text)

fields.name: award
fields.description: the specific award (data format: text)

fields.name: series
fields.description: the name of the Law & Order series that has been nominated (data format: text)

fields.name: episode_id
fields.description: the id of the episode that has been nominated (data format: text)

fields.name: person_id
fields.description: the id of the person that has been nominated (data format: text)

fields.name: role
fields.description: the role that has been nominated (data format: text)

fields.name: result
fields.description: the nomination result Nominee / Winner commonsense evidence: 'Winner' means that the award was actually received. (data format: text)

fields.name: episode_id
fields.description: the id of the episode to which the credit information pertains (data format: text)

fields.name: person_id
fields.description: the id of the person to which the credit information pertains (data format: text)

fields.name: category
fields.description: the kind of credit being recognized (data format: text)

fields.name: role
fields.description: the role for which the person is being recognized If the credit is for an actor, this is the name of the character he or she portrayed (Dan Florek plays Donald Craven). Otherwise, this is the production role (producer, sound editor). (data format: text)

fields.name: credited
fields.description: whether the credit was displayed in the credits at the end of the episode commonsense evidence: A person may fill a role in an episode, but not show up in the on-screen credits. In this case, the work is said to be "uncredited." (data format: text)

fields.name: episode_id
fields.description: the id of the episode (data format: text)

fields.name: stars
fields.description: a number between 1 and 10 indicating how much the viewer enjoyed the episode commonsense evidence: The higher the number, the more the episode was enjoyed (data format: integer)

fields.name: votes
fields.description: The total number of viewers that gave the specific episode the number of stars indicated in the "stars" column (data format: integer)

fields.name: percent
fields.description: The percent of viewers that gave the specific episode the number of stars indicated in the "stars" column (data format: real)
